busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Short gloss misses the second sense ('concurrido' for places).

busy-adj-c3c2275e.quote: Usa 'busy' para describir a una persona que tiene mucho trabajo o una agenda llena.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.fix: Usa 'busy' con '-ing' (sin 'to') para decir en qué estás ocupado: 'I am busy working'.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Note [0] merely restates sense [0] and ignores sense [1] (places).

busy-adj-c3c2275e.quote: Un lugar donde hay mucha gente o mucha actividad.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.fix: Dicho de un lugar, donde hay mucha gente o mucha actividad.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Phrased as a noun ('Un lugar...') instead of an adjective definition.

ask-verb-1acc9c10.why: 'interrogar' means to interrogate formally (as note 1 itself explains for 'question'), not 'ask'.

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: To ask a question or make a demand or request (used with certain nouns). | to ask, to pose, to make
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: Very common light-verb collocation at A1/A2 (eine Frage stellen, einen Antrag stellen).

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.quote: Stellen specifically implies the object stands on its base.
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: Do not confuse stellen with legen (to lay flat) or setzen (to seat someone or sit down).
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: The second sentence repeats note [0] and sense [0] without adding new information.

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: The top covering of a building.
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.fix: The top covering of a building or vehicle.
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: Broaden to include vehicle roofs after merging senses[1].

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: The upper interior surface of a space, like a car interior or a tunnel.
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: A car roof is the same sense; interior ceilings are 'Decke', not 'Dach'.
'Top' is not a standard translation of 'Dach'.

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: While 'Dach' most commonly refers to the structural roof of a building, it is also
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.fix: The plural is 'die Dächer'. Do not confuse with 'die Decke' (the interior ceiling of a room).
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: Current note is filler and contradicts senses; learners need the umlaut plural and 'Decke' distinction.

door-noun-39cd983e.quote: pero también de forma figurada para oportunidades.
door-noun-39cd983e.fix: Se usa a menudo en expresiones como 'next door' (al lado) o 'out of doors' (al aire libre).
door-noun-39cd983e.why: The note mentions a figurative meaning ('opportunity') not included in the senses, and restates senses[0].

box-noun-fb138ba4.fix: Cuadro o espacio pequeño en una página o pantalla donde se escribe o se marca algo. | casilla, recuadro, cuadro
box-noun-fb138ba4.why: Missing the everyday sense of a checkbox or text field on a form or screen.
'caseta' (booth/stall) is not covered by the entry's senses.

box-noun-fb138ba4.quote: La palabra 'box' se refiere principalmente a una caja con lados planos, pero también puede
box-noun-fb138ba4.why: Note merely restates the definitions; a note on the '-es' plural is more useful.

letter-noun-ea13e543.quote: La palabra 'letter' tiene dos significados muy comunes: un mensaje escrito (carta) y un símbolo
letter-noun-ea13e543.why: Merely restates the two senses and glosses already shown in the entry.

letter-noun-ea13e543.quote: La palabra gato empieza con la letra c.
letter-noun-ea13e543.fix: La palabra «cat» empieza con la letra «c».
letter-noun-ea13e543.why: Translating the mentioned English word 'cat' as 'gato' makes the sentence false.

laugh-verb-67b08ddd.why: 'carcajada' is a noun meaning, but this entry is only for the verb 'laugh'.

hair-noun-ebe4b0af.fix: Cada uno de los hilos delgados que crecen en la piel de las personas o de los animales. | pelo, cabello
hair-noun-ebe4b0af.why: Missing the countable sense for a single strand of hair (e.g. 'a gray hair').
As the note states, 'pelo' is also the most common everyday translation for body hair.

hair-noun-ebe4b0af.fix: Cuando se refiere al conjunto del pelo, 'hair' es incontable y se usa en singular ('Her hair is long', no 'hairs'). Solo se usa en plural ('hairs') para hablar de pelos individuales ('I found two hairs in my soup').
hair-noun-ebe4b0af.why: Spanish learners need to know 'hair' is uncountable in English unlike plural 'pelos/cabellos'.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Se usa tanto para el contacto telefónico como para gritar el nombre de alguien desde
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Para pedir la presencia de un profesional o servicio, se usa directamente el objeto («call a doctor», «call a taxi», «call the police»).
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Merely restates senses [0] and [1] without adding useful usage or grammar information.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Por favor llama su nombre para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Por favor, grita su nombre para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: "Llamar su nombre" is an unnatural calque in Spanish; "gritar/decir su nombre" is natural.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: They call the new park Green Valley.
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: They call the new baby their little angel.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Contains a place name ("Green Valley"), violating the rule against names of places.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Llaman al nuevo parque Valle Verde.
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Llaman al nuevo bebé su pequeño ángel.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Update translation to match the corrected, name-free example.

museum-noun-13e50ed9.quote: donde se dice 'museo' con acento en la última sílaba, en inglés el acento fuerte
museum-noun-13e50ed9.fix: Al igual que en español ('mu-SE-o'), en inglés el acento recae en la segunda sílaba: /mjuˈziːəm/.
museum-noun-13e50ed9.why: Spanish 'museo' is stressed on the penultimate syllable (mu-SE-o), not the last syllable.

cough-noun-7995d2db.quote: Es importante notar que 'cough' puede funcionar tanto como sustantivo ('a cough') como verbo ('to
cough-noun-7995d2db.fix: La combinación «gh» al final de esta palabra se pronuncia como una «f» (/kɔf/). Además, «cough» funciona tanto como sustantivo («a cough») como verbo («to cough»).
cough-noun-7995d2db.why: Learners need a note on the irregular spelling-to-sound correspondence of '-ough' (/ɔf/).

line-noun-f3348969.fix: Serie horizontal de palabras o letras en un texto. | línea, renglón
line-noun-f3348969.why: Common A2 meaning (a line of text/poem or actor's line) is missing.

line-noun-f3348969.fix: Conexión telefónica o ruta de transporte público (como de tren o metro). | línea
line-noun-f3348969.why: Common A2 meanings (phone line, subway/train line) are missing.

line-noun-f3348969.quote: Usa 'line' para hablar de personas esperando en fila (ej. en el supermercado).
line-noun-f3348969.fix: Combinaciones frecuentes para hacer fila: 'wait in line' o 'stand in line' (esperar en la fila).
line-noun-f3348969.why: Restates sense[0]; teaching collocations 'wait/stand in line' is much more useful.

line-noun-f3348969.quote: Para una marca dibujada o una línea geométrica, también se usa 'line'.
line-noun-f3348969.why: Merely repeats sense[1] without adding grammatical or usage information.

name-noun-a25a0089.why: 'name' alone does not mean 'apellido' (last name), and sense 1 is 'reputación'.

name-noun-a25a0089.quote: así como a su apellido o nombre completo.
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Se usa tanto para el nombre de pila como para el nombre completo. Para «apellido» se dice «last name» o «surname».
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Alone, 'name' means first or full name; 'surname'/'last name' is needed for 'apellido'.

name-noun-a25a0089.quote: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona.
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona, animal, cosa o lugar.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Too narrow: things, places, and animals also have names.

name-noun-a25a0089.fix: What is the name of this street?
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Examples must not contain personal names.

name-noun-a25a0089.fix: ¿Cuál es el nombre de esta calle?
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Match the updated example without a personal name.

snake-noun-d1d756ef.quote: En contextos informales, a veces se usa 'serpent' en literatura
snake-noun-d1d756ef.fix: Es la palabra común y cotidiana para referirse a este reptil ('serpent' es mucho más formal o literario).
snake-noun-d1d756ef.why: Contradictory phrasing calling literary contexts informal.

snake-noun-d1d756ef.fix: Reptil de cuerpo largo y estrecho, sin patas y cubierto de escamas.
snake-noun-d1d756ef.why: All snakes have scales, not just 'often'; 'animal reptil' is slightly redundant.

smell-verb-908c9ead.fix: Tener un olor particular, bueno o malo.
smell-verb-908c9ead.why: 'Aroma' in Spanish implies a pleasant smell, whereas 'smell' is used for any smell.
'Oler' alone is the main gloss (e.g., 'oler bien/mal'); 'oler a' is for 'smell like/of'.

smell-verb-908c9ead.fix: Cuando se usa para describir un olor ('oler bien/mal'), 'smell' no se usa en formas continuas (di 'It smells good', no 'It is smelling good').
smell-verb-908c9ead.why: Compares verb 'smell' with noun 'scent' in a verb entry; stative verb grammar is needed.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: Lugar donde el agua subterránea brota de la tierra de forma natural. | manantial, fuente
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Missing the very common everyday meaning of a natural water spring.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: A spring in the old mattress is broken.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: 'Lost its spring' means uncountable elasticity/bounce, not a metal coil.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: Un resorte del colchón viejo está roto.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Mistranslates the idiom 'lost its spring' and updates to match the fixed example.

spring-noun-5b622de6.quote: La palabra 'spring' tiene varios significados muy comunes en inglés: la estación del año...
spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: Como estación del año, se usa con la preposición 'in' y con o sin artículo ('in spring' o 'in the spring').
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: merely restates the glosses already listed in the senses.

a-veces-adv-566ce858.quote: Used to express that an action happens occasionally but not always.
a-veces-adv-566ce858.why: Merely restates the definition and glosses without adding useful information.

train-noun-a4d69b7d.quote: Una serie de personas, animales o cosas que se mueven en fila o seguidos.
train-noun-a4d69b7d.why: Too literary/rare for an A2 beginner; only the vehicle sense is needed at this level.
'Cola' corresponds to the trailing part of a dress, not a moving line of people/animals.

train-noun-a4d69b7d.quote: Aunque 'train' se traduce principalmente como 'tren', también puede usarse para describir una serie...
train-noun-a4d69b7d.fix: 'Train' también se usa como verbo (entrenar o capacitar), y en la expresión común 'train of thought' (hilo de pensamientos).
train-noun-a4d69b7d.why: Merely restates the senses and mentions 'cola de un vestido', which is not covered.

stomach-noun-e0b3137c.quote: Aunque 'stomach' se usa para el órgano interno, es muy común usarlo de forma coloquial
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.why: Restates the two senses already given, and using 'stomach' for 'belly' is neutral, not colloquial.

tall-adj-9bc90422.quote: De un objeto que tiene una gran extensión vertical.
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Physical height of people and vertical objects is one sense, plus missing measurement sense.

tall-adj-9bc90422.fix: Que tiene una altura determinada o medida. | de altura, alto
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Missing the common A1/A2 measurement sense (e.g., 'six feet tall', 'How tall are you?').

tall-adj-9bc90422.quote: Usa 'tall' para describir personas o cosas que tienen mucha altura vertical.
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage contrast.

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Se escuchaba una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.fix: Se veía una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: 'Escuchar' means to hear; light is seen ('se veía'), not heard.

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Used to describe both physical weakness and weak things like a faint voice or a
debil-adj-3af279b9.fix: Invariable in gender (un hombre débil, una voz débil); plural is débiles.
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: Merely repeats the two senses; a note on gender invariability is more helpful.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: To feel a very strong and deep love for someone.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: To feel deep affection or romantic passion for someone.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Circular definition uses 'love' to define 'to love'.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: to like someone very much, adore, love
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Most common gloss 'love' should come first; 'someone' excludes things/activities.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: Ella dice que ama bailar los fines de semana.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: In Spain, 'amar' + infinitive is unnatural (learners should use 'encantar').

el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.quote: Coins and paper notes used to buy things and pay for services.
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.fix: What you earn, save, and use to buy things and pay for services, including cash and money in a bank.
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.why: Too narrow; 'dinero' includes non-physical money in bank accounts, not just coins and notes.
'wealth' is not covered as a distinct sense in the entry.

el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.quote: Do not confuse it with change or coins (la moneda), though both relate to payments.
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.fix: For loose change, use 'el cambio' or 'la suelta'; for a single coin or a currency, use 'la moneda'.
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.why: 'La moneda' means 'coin' or 'currency', not 'change' (which is 'el cambio' or 'suelto').

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.quote: To hand something over to someone, or to provide an object to someone.
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: To hand or provide something to someone, or to cause an emotion or action.
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: Too narrow; excludes abstract objects like information, advice, or emotions ('dar miedo').

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: To teach a class or study a subject in school. | teach, cover, take (a class)
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: Very common everyday sense in Peninsular Spanish ('dar clase', 'dar un tema').

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: To look out onto or face a place (used with 'a'). | face, overlook, lead to
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: Common A2 everyday sense for describing rooms and buildings ('la ventana da a la calle').

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: 'Dar' is irregular in the first-person singular present ('doy') and takes regular -er/-ir endings in the preterite ('di', 'diste', 'dio').
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: A1/A2 learners plainly need a note on the high-frequency irregular forms 'doy' and 'di'.

el-reloj-noun-3427c7b1.why: Adding 'wristwatch' makes the distinction from 'clock' unmistakable.

el-reloj-noun-3427c7b1.quote: In Spanish, 'el reloj' covers both what you put on the wall and what you

el-reloj-noun-3427c7b1.why: The note merely restates the two senses; teach the compounds that distinguish them instead.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: Note that 'museo' is masculine, so use 'el' or 'un'.
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Restates the regular masculine gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: In Spain, you might hear people use the plural 'museos' if they are visiting a
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Trivial observation about regular plural formation and contains a place name (Madrid).

el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.why: The direct translation 'minute' is the most natural gloss here (as in the example).

el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.quote: Used exactly like the English 'minute' for both time and short moments.
el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.why: Merely restates the two senses and glosses already shown in the entry.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: El código de vestido para el evento es formal.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.fix: Gastamos mucho dinero en comida y vestido.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: 'Dress code' in Spanish is 'código de vestimenta' or 'etiqueta', not 'código de vestido'.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: The dress code for the event is formal.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.fix: We spend a lot of money on food and clothing.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: Update translation to match the corrected Spanish example.

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.label: place-name
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de Madrid.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.fix: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de la costa.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Examples must not contain names of places ('Madrid').

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.label: place-name
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: My family lives in a small town near Madrid.

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Examples must not contain names of places ('Madrid').

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: While 'familia' usually refers to parents, children, and close relatives living together, it is also

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Merely restates the definition and glosses without adding useful grammatical or usage information.

la-primavera-noun-8de86356.quote: or contraction 'en primavera' (in spring) without an article.
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.fix: Normally used with the feminine article 'la', except in the phrase 'en primavera' (in spring), which takes no article.
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.why: 'En primavera' is a prepositional phrase, not a contraction.

la-universidad-noun-23f53449.quote: In Spain and Latin America, 'universidad' refers to higher education institutions
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.fix: In informal speech, 'la universidad' is often shortened to 'la uni'.
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.why: The note merely restates the definition and offers no useful usage information.

lleno-adj-066a8598.why: Standard Castilian phonological representation distinguishes /ʎ/ for 'll', or notes yeísmo alongside /ˈʎeno/.

lleno-adj-066a8598.quote: Use 'lleno' for containers, rooms, or people who have eaten enough.
lleno-adj-066a8598.fix: Normally used with the verb 'estar' and the preposition 'de' ('estar lleno de' = to be full of).
lleno-adj-066a8598.why: Merely restates the three senses; should explain grammar ('estar' + 'lleno de') instead.

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.label: example.proper-noun
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: Mi hermano vive en otra ciudad.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Examples must not contain names of places.

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.quote: Any male or female person who shares the same parents as another.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: (in plural 'hermanos', or in general questions) brothers and sisters; a sibling.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Singular 'hermano' does not mean a female sibling; this use is mainly plural or generic.

no-expression-d81d4edd.quote: Used as a standard negation to express refusal or disagreement.
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Merely restates the definition of sense 0 without adding usage information.

no-expression-d81d4edd.quote: you often use 'no' twice in a sentence
no-expression-d81d4edd.fix: Unlike in English, Spanish uses double negatives: 'no' goes before the verb when a negative word like 'nada' (nothing) or 'nadie' (nobody) follows it, as in 'No quiero nada' (I don't want anything).
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Claims 'no' is used twice, but the example uses 'no' and 'nada'.

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.why: As an adverb alone, 'tarde' means 'late', not 'in the afternoon' (por la tarde).

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.quote: Used as an adverb meaning 'late', as in 'Llego tarde' (I am arriving late).
tarde-adv-d70fcb11.fix: Do not confuse with the feminine noun 'la tarde' (afternoon, evening), as in 'por la tarde' (in the afternoon).

caro-adj-b40d396d.quote: In some contexts, 'caro' can also mean 'dear' in an emotional sense
caro-adj-b40d396d.fix: Remove this note; the literary meaning 'dear' is not among the senses, and the example given actually shows figurative cost, not emotional affection.

rico-adj-44bbcf17.quote: Do not confuse this with 'rico' in a social context, which can sometimes imply
rico-adj-44bbcf17.why: Compares the word to itself and discusses a shade of Sense 0 not needing separation.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: 'Tomorrow' is the adverbial or masculine noun meaning, not covered in the feminine noun senses.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.quote: A period of time or an entire day considered in relation to a specific event
la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: Still means the morning; 'entire day' in the definition is also false.

adj-0eff005c.why: shortGloss includes 'light-colored', which is not in the senses and contradicts note [0].

adj-0eff005c.quote: Use белый for things that are literally the color of snow
adj-0eff005c.fix: Белый means 'white' (like snow or milk), and is also used in fixed phrases like белый хлеб (white bread) and белое вино (white wine).
adj-0eff005c.why: Белый is also used for things not literally snow-white, like white bread or white wine.

adj-0eff005c.quote: The color of snow or milk.
adj-0eff005c.fix: Having the color of snow or milk.
adj-0eff005c.why: Noun phrase definition for an adjective; should be an adjectival phrase.

adj-0eff005c.quote: Зимой весь город стал белый от снега.
adj-0eff005c.fix: Зимой весь город стал белым от снега.
adj-0eff005c.why: After 'стал' in the past tense, the instrumental case 'белым' is much more natural.

adj-2eb76e52.quote: Use быстрый when talking about speed in movement or action, such as a fast car
adj-2eb76e52.why: Restates the definitions and glosses without adding grammatical or usage information.

adj-342a5dda.quote: Used to describe people or animals that show kindness and a warm attitude toward others.
adj-342a5dda.why: Merely restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.quote: Water sprayed over the body to wash.
la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.fix: An act of washing the body under sprayed water.
la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.why: The example and reference show this sense is the act of showering, not the water.

noun-0a176f48.fix: Has a fleeting vowel -е- in all declined forms (genitive: кашля) and is usually used in the singular.
noun-0a176f48.why: Learners need to know about the fleeting vowel -е- in declined forms (кашля, кашлю).

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: En Estados Unidos se utiliza principalmente la palabra 'juice' para referirse a cualquier bebida
juice-noun-ba520c0a.fix: Normalmente es un sustantivo incontable (some juice, a glass of juice).
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Merely restates senses[0] and implies 'juice' is a US-specific word.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: En España, es mucho más común utilizar la palabra 'zumo' para referirse a la
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Explains Spanish regional vocabulary ('zumo') rather than the English headword.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: La palabra 'juice' también puede usarse de forma figurada para hablar de la energía
juice-noun-ba520c0a.fix: En el sentido de 'energía' o 'batería' (sentido 2), es de uso coloquial.
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Merely repeats senses[1] without adding new usage or register information.
Omits the second sense present in the entry.

noun-06b6922b.quote: While this word is technically a noun, it functions like an adjective (adjectival noun).
noun-06b6922b.fix: 'Взрослый' is also an adjective meaning 'adult'. As a noun, it declines like an adjective (feminine 'взрослая', plural 'взрослые').
noun-06b6922b.why: It is originally an adjective used as a noun (substantivized adjective), not the reverse.

noun-06b6922b.quote: It is the standard, neutral way to refer to someone who is not a child.
noun-06b6922b.why: Only restates the definition and the neutral register field.

noun-63b38367.quote: A container of cloth or plastic you carry things in.
noun-63b38367.fix: A flexible container with handles or a strap, made of leather, cloth, or plastic, used for carrying things.
noun-63b38367.why: Bags (especially handbags) are very often made of leather, not only cloth or plastic.

noun-83a7e7c6.why: Uses Polish letter 'ł' (U+0142) instead of IPA velarized l 'ɫ' (U+026B) or plain 'l'.

noun-91420c9c.quote: Used specifically for the institution where people receive medical treatment and stay in beds.
noun-91420c9c.why: Merely restates the definition of a hospital, which is already clear from note [1].

noun-980d1ea3.quote: Do not confuse this with 'авиация' (aviation), which refers to the industry
noun-980d1ea3.fix: Use 'на самолёте' (prepositional case) or 'самолётом' (instrumental case) to mean 'by plane'.
noun-980d1ea3.why: Learners do not confuse 'самолёт' and 'авиация'; a note on preposition/case usage is much more useful.

noun-e020a647.label: missing stress mark
noun-e020a647.quote: Note the stress shift in plural: 'река' becomes 'ре́ки' (rivers)
noun-e020a647.fix: Note the stress shift in the plural: 'река́' becomes 'ре́ки' (rivers) and the genitive plural is 'рек'.
noun-e020a647.why: A note explaining a stress shift should mark the stress on the singular form too.

noun-c32f2ada.quote: In Russian, 'море' refers specifically to the sea. Be careful not to confuse it with
noun-c32f2ada.fix: Use 'на море' (not 'в море') when talking about going to the seaside or being on vacation at the coast.
noun-c32f2ada.why: Restates the gloss; 'море' and 'озеро' are not easily confused.

noun-d65f1aed.quote: Used for both physical pain and emotional suffering.
noun-d65f1aed.fix: Ends in the soft sign -ь, which can be masculine or feminine; боль is feminine (сильная боль).
noun-d65f1aed.why: Restates the two senses; a note on the -ь feminine declension is much more useful.

noun-f29d6dec.quote: In Russian culture, the uzhin is typically the main meal of the day
noun-f29d6dec.fix: ужин is the evening meal; traditionally in Russian culture, обед (the midday meal) is the largest meal of the day, though in modern work life ужин is often when the family eats together.
noun-f29d6dec.why: Traditionally in Russian culture, обед (midday) is the main meal, not ужин.

verb-62298af6.quote: This verb describes carrying something by holding it or wearing it as you move somewhere.
verb-62298af6.fix: 'нести' is unidirectional (carrying in one direction right now); its multidirectional pair is 'носить', and its perfective is 'понести'.
verb-62298af6.why: 'нести' does not mean wearing clothes ('носить' does), and the motion-verb pair is missing.

verb-d97247f1.fix: Takes the dative case for the listener (кому?), the accusative case (что?) or 'о' + prepositional case (о чём?) for the topic, and contrasts with 'говорить' (to speak/say in general) and 'сказать' (to say briefly).
verb-d97247f1.why: Learners need the case governance and contrast with 'говорить'/'сказать', both translated as 'tell'.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: First velar stop is voiceless /k/, not voiced /ɡ/.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.quote: Bakmak is a very versatile verb. While its primary meaning is to look,
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.fix: 'Bakmak' takes the dative case (-(y)e/-(y)a) for the object being looked at or cared for.
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Only restates the glosses; replace with the crucial dative case requirement.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.fix: To check, examine, or attend to something (such as a door, phone, or patient). | to check, to have a look at, to see to
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Everyday A2 usage (e.g., 'kapıya bakmak' to answer the door, 'telefona bakmak').

verb-0851f175.quote: to take; to catch; to rent
verb-0851f175.fix: to take; to rent; to borrow
verb-0851f175.why: 'to catch' is not covered in the senses.

verb-0851f175.fix: To take something from someone or a library with the intention of returning it. | to borrow, to take out
verb-0851f175.why: Everyday A1/A2 sense (e.g., брать книгу в библиотеке) is missing.

verb-0851f175.fix: Он часто берёт книги с этой полки.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the perfective partner 'взять' instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.quote: Мы решили взять машину напрокат на выходные.
verb-0851f175.fix: В отпуске мы всегда берём машину напрокат.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the perfective partner 'взять' instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.fix: Брать has an irregular present tense stem with an inserted -е-: я беру́, ты берёшь, они беру́т. In the past tense, the stress shifts to the ending in the feminine form: брал, брала́, бра́ли.
verb-0851f175.why: Learners need the non-obvious irregular present stem (бер-) of this core verb.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: To remain inactive, dormant, or unresponsive.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.fix: remove (or replace with the informal sense: To be unaware of what is happening around you. | be asleep at the wheel, be oblivious)
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Figurative 'uyumak' means being oblivious/inattentive, not dormant mechanisms; marginal for A2.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Proje üzerinde çalışanlar biraz uyudu ama şimdi tekrar hızlandılar.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Unnatural Turkish; 'uyumak' is not used this way to mean pausing work on a project.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Uyumak is the standard verb for sleeping, but it can also describe mechanisms or systems
uyumak-verb-56fff049.fix: Do not confuse 'uyumak' (to sleep) with 'uymak' (to fit, to suit, to obey).
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: False claim about mechanisms/systems; 'uyumak' vs 'uymak' is the key learner confusion.

noun-8c1fb7b7.quote: На улице к нему подошёл незнакомец и спросил время.
noun-8c1fb7b7.fix: На улице к нему подошёл незнакомец и спросил, который час.
noun-8c1fb7b7.why: Russian normally uses 'спросил, который час' or 'сколько времени', not 'спросил время'.

verb-ac9e5c2f.quote: Followed immediately by the instrumental case (in Russian, nouns take the ending -е or -ой).
verb-ac9e5c2f.fix: Followed by the preposition в (or во) + prepositional case (e.g., нуждаться в помощи).
verb-ac9e5c2f.why: Нуждаться takes в + prepositional case, not the instrumental case; -е is a prepositional ending.

verb-843f487d.quote: to eat; to drink; to suffer
verb-843f487d.fix: to eat; to take (medicine); to suffer
verb-843f487d.why: Standard Mandarin uses 喝 to drink; listing 'to drink' for 吃 misleads beginners.

verb-843f487d.quote: Besides food, 吃 is used for drinks that involve a spoon or are considered meals,
verb-843f487d.fix: Besides solid food, 吃 is also used for taking medicine (吃药) and in some fixed expressions.
verb-843f487d.why: Pills and noodles are not drinks; soups and porridge use 喝 in standard Mandarin.

verb-843f487d.quote: To consume a liquid or take medication.
verb-843f487d.fix: To take medicine or other substances.
verb-843f487d.why: In standard Mandarin, 吃 does not generally mean to consume liquids.

kupowac-verb-781f5553.quote: Muszę kupować świeże owoce na targowisku.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.fix: Często kupuję świeże owoce na targu.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.why: 'Muszę kupować' is awkward without habitual context; 'targ' is much more natural than 'targowisko'.
